label: copy-phase echo of l (mid/late recall), strongest when next output is 1
predicate: (phase == 2) & (in_tok == tok("l")) & (recall_idx >= 3) & isin(out_tok, [tok("1"), tok("z"), tok("x"), tok("n"), tok("h"), tok("l"), tok("f"), tok("c")])
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases) and only on repeated tokens (in_first=0). About 94% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is l. It needs recall_idx >= 3 (t=10-13 hold most mass) and is weighted toward long sequences (L=8-9). Smaller secondary activations occur on inputs 1 and x. Magnitude depends on the token being output: the top examples are almost all l followed by 1 (out_tok=1 gets 39% of mass, lift 16x), then z, x, n, h, f, c. On its own, in_tok=l & recall_idx>=3 gets 93% of mass but only 13% precision: most copy-phase l echoes stay silent. Restricting out_tok to {1,z,x,n,h,l,f,c} raises dev precision to 0.38 (F1 0.48, mass recall 0.79). Other tokens tried (m, 0, s, i) lowered F1. Does not fire on the first occurrence of a token, on recall_idx<=1, or on letters outside l/1/x. The remaining gating among l echoes was not captured.
